chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:

Abu al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn wrote to Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him) via me: 'May I be sacrificed for you! Your followers are differing regarding the Fajr prayer. Among them is one who prays when the first dawn rises elongated vertically in the sky, and among them is one who prays when it spreads horizontally at the bottom of the horizon and becomes clear. I do not know the better of the two times to pray in it. So if you see fit to teach me the better of the two times and define it for me, and how I should act when the moon is present and the dawn cannot be distinguished until it turns red and morning comes, and how I should act with clouds, and what the limit of that is during journey and at home — I will do so, God willing.'

So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting, and I read it: 'The dawn — may God have mercy on you — is the white horizontal line. It is not the vertical whiteness. So do not pray, whether on a journey or at home, until you distinguish it clearly.'
For God, Blessed and Exalted, has not left His creation in doubt about this. He said: "Eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread of the dawn." [2:187]
The white thread is the horizontal one, by which eating and drinking become forbidden during the fast, and similarly it is that by which prayer becomes obligatory.

key_terms.الخيط الأبيض المعترض: The horizontal white thread — the true dawn (al-fajr al-sadiq), as opposed to the false dawn (al-fajr al-kadhib) which appears vertical
key_terms.الفجر الأول المستطيل: The first elongated dawn — the false dawn, appearing as a vertical streak of light before true dawn
key_terms.بخطه: In his own handwriting — signifying a direct personal response from the Imam, giving the ruling special authority
key_terms.موالوك: Those loyal to you; followers in the Imam's wilaya — a term reflecting the Shia concept of devotion to the Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the correct time for Fajr prayer according to Imam al-Jawad — the vertical or horizontal dawn?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written correspondence between a follower and Imam al-Jawad (AS), the ninth Imam, concerning the onset time for the Fajr prayer. A companion wrote to the Imam asking him to clarify which of two observable dawn phenomena — the first vertical elongation of light in the sky versus the horizontal spread of light at the horizon — marks the correct prayer time. The Imam responded in his own handwriting, definitively identifying the horizontal white thread of dawn (al-fajr al-sadiq, true dawn) as the correct marker, not the false dawn (al-fajr al-kadhib) that appears vertically. He grounded his ruling in Quran 2:187, which uses this precise metaphor of distinguishing the white thread from the black thread. The same marker that ends permissible eating and drinking during Ramadan also obligates the Fajr prayer — applying uniformly in travel and residence alike.
